newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica halts Placer Dome gold exploration.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica halts Placer Dome gold exploration.

text.p: Costa Rica has ordered Placer Dome Inc. of Canada to suspend some of its gold exploration in the north of the country because of environmental damage, a government spokesman said Friday.
Costa Rica is widely recognised as the most aggressive country in Central America in protecting its tropical forests and other natural resources, largely to fuel a booming ecotourism industry.

"The company's exploration and mining activities have eliminated parts of woodland and moved quantities of earth that have accumulated without adequate control," Rene Castro, Minister of the Environment and Mining, said.

Castro also said Placer Dome, based in Vancouver, British Columbia, had harmed the countryside and caused substantial damage to the ground, flora and fauna. Among the complaints was that Placer's drilling at the site was creating noise that disturbed local wildlife.
In Vancouver, Placer Dome spokesman Hugh Leggatt said the company had caused no environmental damage at Cerro Crucitas, the site in question, and said he was surprised by the government order.
"This came without warning. ... We see no reason for it," he said.
The government granted Placer Dome three months to take measures to reduce and offset environmental damage caused and to change working practices so as not to repeat the damage.
Placer Dome began operations in Costa Rica, near the border with Nicaragua, in 1993 on about 5,000 acres under a government concession.
The government ordered the company to stop exploring in 250 acres where Placer's activities are concentrated.

Placer said it believed it was in compliance with an environmental impact statement previously agreed with the government. Leggatt said the suspension order appeared to stem from "subjective interpretations" of that plan by the government.

Studies are being conducted on the Cerro Crucitas project to determine if a mine would be economically viable. Placer has so far identified 2.2 million ounces of gold and invested $20 million there, the spokesman said.
